rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Chap. LVII. Of Commanders in Armies, their abilities, fidelity, and whether by them Victory may be had yea or not
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Chapter LVII considers army commanders, their abilities, fidelity and claims about success.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Original PDF414 / printed380 below divider. Above it remains Chapter LVI; do not include.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: consider well all the twelve houses and their proper Significators
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Lilly instructs the historical reader to consider all twelve houses and the planets signifying them.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: A source instruction, not a complete or empirically validated algorithm.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: make the ascendant Significator of the querent, and his Lord
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The ascendant and its lord signify the querent's party.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not the same assignment as the opponent's house.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: let the seventh & his Lord shew the opposite parties or Adversaries
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The seventh house and lord are assigned to opposing parties, including those who might relieve the besieged.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The seventh includes defenders' supporters only as historical chart symbolism.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: let the eight be their Seconds or Friends
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The eighth house is designated for the opposing parties' seconds or friends.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Turned-house semantics may be different from ordinary direct eighth-house meaning.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: ninth their third House, and so all the other Houses in order
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The opponent's third-house interests are assigned to the ninth and the other houses are turned analogously.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: No hidden numerical weighting or additional house content supplied.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortune in the ascendant, or beholding the house with square or opposition
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A malefic in the ascendant or aspecting it by square/opposition is a qualifying condition for an unfavorable querent reading.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Distinguish residency from hard aspects; no orb is specified.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: will not manage their matters well, or prosecute the Warre discreetely
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author predicts poor judgment or management by the querent's party under those conditions.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Historical narrative only; not a finding about any real commander.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: an Infortune in the ascendant, or being Lord of the ascendant
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text also names a malefic as first lord as a related but distinct test of the querent's cause.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Continuation crosses PDF414 to 415.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: no great justice on the querent's part ... no cause to begin the Warre
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He questions the justification of the querent's quarrel or war in that state.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: A historical moral assertion, not a validated judgment of actual political legitimacy.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: good Planet be in the ascendant ... sextile or trine
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The source offers a good planet in the ascendant or a favorable sextile/trine to it as a contrasting condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The OR alternatives should not be silently collapsed into conjunction.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: a good ground or cause on the querent's behalfe
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Lilly says those favorable configurations imply a just cause for the querent.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: No empirical link between chart and legitimate warfare established.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortune be in the second ... not Lord of the second (or have Exaltation in the Signe)
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: An unfavorable planet in the second is qualified by its NOT being lord of the second nor exalted in the sign.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The original parenthetic clause is exception-sensitive; precise scope between lordship/exaltation kept source-native.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: behold the second with square or opposition
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A square or opposition aspect to the second is an additional condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Original text refers back to the just-described infortune; no generic second-house hard aspect.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: there will be no Warre ... if any be, querent shall have the worst
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author speculates either that no war occurs or that the querent fares worst if fighting occurs.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Mutually conditional outcomes; do not conflate no-war and defeat predictions.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: a Fortune in that house, or aspecting it
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A benefic planet in the second or aspecting the second is an alternative configuration.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: No stated complete aspect list or numeric dignity score.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: shewes the contrary
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text supplies only a brief 'contrary' response to the adverse second-house condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Do not invent a deterministic affirmative victory rule or interval.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortune ... in the third, and Mars ... strong
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A strong Mars as unfavorable planet in the third is identified as an exceptional source condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Mars must be the third-house malefic AND strong.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: querent is like to have good warlike Provisions
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author associates that particular condition with favorable provisions.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Unverified historical claim; not supply or combat-planning advice.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: say the same if Jupiter be there
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He adds Jupiter in the third as a separate alternative.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Do not require both Mars and Jupiter.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Mars be therein unfortunate
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author contrasts an unfortunate Mars in the third with his earlier strong Mars case.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Polarity and exact third-house antecedent matter.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Army ... Thieves ... seditious ... obey no commands
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He makes unfavorable claims about the soldiers' character, discipline and obedience.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not evidence that any real individual is a thief or disobedient.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortune be in the fourth
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A malefic in the fourth introduces the source's claims about the proposed location.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not a tested tactical evaluation method.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: place where the Warre is ... unfit for the querent's Army
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He judges the location unfavorable for the querent's party.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: This is historic astrological conjecture.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: mountainous ... rough ... Woods ... no passage
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The printed text elaborates with mountains, rough terrain and woods.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Retained as historical text context; not rendered as route or operational advice.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: moyft ... standing waters, Bogs, Rivers or Brooks
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He also describes wet ground and bodies of water in the historical illustration.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: No location-specific modern military recommendation.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Mars be in the fift well dignified, or good aspects ... Fortunes
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The source describes a dignified Mars in fifth or supportive benefic aspects there.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Alternative chart predicates retained; exact numerical dignities not supplied.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Soldiers ... good ... apt for fight ... obedient
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author attributes good fighting quality and obedience to those favorable fifth-house configurations.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: This does not evaluate actual soldiers or support wartime decisions.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortunes posited therein shew contrary qualities
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He offers a converse for unfavorable planets in the fifth.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Abbreviated converse is not independently enumerated into a personality classifier.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Fortunes or [node glyph] be in the sixth
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Benefics or a printed node-like glyph in the sixth are associated with draft animals' serviceability.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The extra glyph is not positively identified.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Carriage-Horse ... serviceable ... fit
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text claims army horses will be serviceable and suitable for their employment.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Historical source-only interpretation.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Mars ... therein well dignified
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Dignified Mars in sixth is a distinct clause about horses.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: This is separate from the fortunate planet clause.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Horse ... fierce, impatient and hard to be governed
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Such a position is said to indicate spirited, hard-to-manage animals.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not an observed case of animal temperament.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Saturn ... sixth without dignities
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Saturn in the sixth without dignity introduces a contrasting assertion.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Exclusion of dignity must be retained.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Horses are old ... not fit for this service
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text associates that Saturn condition with poor horse fitness.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Historical assertion; no veterinary claims inferred.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: a Fortune ... seventh
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A benefic in the seventh is said to signal well-formed instruments and fortifications.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The source connects this to the opponent's characteristics as well.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Canons and great Guns ... faire, sound ... Enemy is no foole
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Lilly claims equipment will function and the opposing side is capable.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Retained as period text, not equipment quality assurance or military advice.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortune be there ... evill aspects to the house
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He contrasts a malefic in seventh or unfavorable aspect with the seventh.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Dignity and aspect qualifiers cannot be omitted.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: enemy weak ... instruments ... no service ... craft and trechery
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He ascribes weakness, poor effectiveness and deceptive conduct in that opposing configuration.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Character accusations and equipment prognosis are unverified.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Fortune be in the eight
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A beneficial planet in the eighth is the first alternative in this source passage.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not stated as a universal life-or-death diagnostic.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: no mortality ... many men wounded ... wounds difficult to cure
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text makes claims about severity of casualties or injury and absence of large battles.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The authorial phrase contains multiple alternatives; no clinical outcome evidence.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Saturn ... therein Retrograde
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A retrograde Saturn in eighth is an express contrasting condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Both planet and retrograde state required.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: many prisoners ... ruine and destruction ... plundering
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Under that contrast the author speculates about prisoners and destructive consequences.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Unverified period-specific claim.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: a Fortune be in the ninth, or have aspect to the house
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The ninth-house indicator includes a fortunate planet in or aspecting that house.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Aspect kind unspecified.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: enemy ... false reports ... false alarums ... witty inventions
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author conjectures that the opposing party may use misleading reports.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: An asserted mental/behavioral inference, not substantiated intelligence.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: a Fortune be in the tenth, or cast sextile or trine thither
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A benefic in tenth or aspecting it by sextile/trine introduces an assessment of the commander.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Planet in house versus aspect are alternatives.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Commander in chiefe ... discreet ... Officers ... expert
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Lilly associates the favorable configuration with command capability and expertise.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: No real-world competence assessment established.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Saturn or [node glyph] ... or Mars any wayes unfortunate
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Saturn, an uncertain printed glyph, or afflicted Mars in tenth gives the contrasting source condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The aspect/dignity extent of 'any wayes unfortunate' is not defined.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Officers ... no judgment ... design overthrown
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He uses insulting characterizations and predicts failure under that condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: This is historical rhetoric, not a true assessment of soldiers.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Fortune be in the eleventh
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A benefic in the eleventh is treated as a favorable commander condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Distinct from eighth/ninth/tenth significations.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Conductors ... good discretion ... expert
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author praises the historical officers' discretion, judgment and discipline.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Unverified personality claim.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortune be in the eleventh
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: An infortune in the eleventh is a separate unfavorable commander condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Does not necessarily imply dishonesty in original wording.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: may be men of fidelity ... but unexperts ... cause suffer
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He specifically distinguishes good intentions/fidelity from a lack of expertise and attributes probable harm to the cause.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: This nuance crosses pages 416→417 and must NOT be flattened into betrayal.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Fortune be in the twelft house
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A benefic in the twelfth is said to refer to preparedness of those opposed to the querent.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The twelfth-house subject changes from the querent to the opposite forces.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: those against whom the Army is to goe ... well provided ... stand it out
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Lilly describes opponents as prepared, united and resolute under that reading.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not a supported modern military forecast.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Infortune be there
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: A malefic in twelfth introduces the contrasting opponent interpretation.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Distinct from its favorable twelfth-house alternative.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: not capable of resisting ... disagree amongst themselves
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text associates the malefic with opponent incapacity and internal disagreement.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not substantiated intelligence about any real force.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Mars be in the twelft house ... [node glyph] be in the twelft
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Mars, or an additional node-like glyph, is listed as a third twelfth-house condition.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Literal printed glyph unresolved; not an identity diagnosis.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: querent may justly suspect trechery
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: Lilly offers suspicion of treachery in that state.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Authorial suspicion must not become a factual allegation.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: consider ... same method ... on the behalf of the Adversary
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He instructs applying a symmetrical house reading to the opposite party.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Source statement, not license to invent unstated converse conditions.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: querent ... ascendant ... opposite house ... quesited
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The opposite/seventh house is assigned to the adversary for the turned-house comparison.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Role reversal across all houses is source-specific.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: every house in order
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author extends the house-turning idea across the twelve houses.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: No numeric scoring rule or detailed mapping table written here.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: If the Armies shall fight.
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: An unnumbered section about whether the opposing parties meet in battle remains within Chapter LVII.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Do NOT incorrectly start Chapter LVIII at this heading.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: ascendant and his Lord, the Moon and Lord of the seventh
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text explicitly compares ascendant and its lord, Moon and seventh lord for that question.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Keep roles distinct from earlier fifth/eighth house claims.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: corporally joyned in any angle
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The author gives an angular bodily conjunction as a condition for possible fighting.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Not every unqualified conjunction; angular placement is explicit.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: then it seems the Armies will fight
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He predicts a battle under the preceding angular union.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Original phrasing 'seems' is qualitative and not empirically calibrated.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: if there be no conjunction ... square or opposition
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: If no corporeal conjunction, the author checks square/opposition between the two lords.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Explicit negative prerequisite applies.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: they will also then fight
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: He makes an additional battle forecast under that hard-aspect configuration.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Historical conjecture only.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: if this happen not ... any Planet transferre the light ... square or opposition
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: If neither preceding indicator occurs, a third planet transferring light by square/opposition is considered.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The third-planet translation is conditional on earlier branches failing.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: with or without Reception
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The original explicitly allows transfer of light with or without reception.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Do not make mutual reception a mandatory prerequisite for this test.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: there will be a fight betwixt them
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The text conjectures fighting following the qualifying light transfer.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: The separate heavy-planet exception follows immediately.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: more ponderous ... receive that Planet who transfers their light
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: If the heavier of the two main planets receives the transferring planet, the source overrides the prior fight reading.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Critical reception-direction exception; no numeric definition of 'ponderous' given.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: no fight ... all things will be composed lightly
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: With that reception exception the author instead forecasts easy settlement.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Mutually exclusive result relative to immediate preceding translation-of-light branch.

rules.source_anchor_short_not_diplomatic: Chap. LVIII. If the Querent have open Enemies, or any Adversaries
rules.original_author_claim_paraphrase: The following chapter on enemies begins below the physical divider on PDF417/printed383.
rules.source_qualifiers_and_limits: Navigation marker only, LVIII assertions are excluded from this Chapter LVII archive.
